extraFacts.fact: Column load is the compressive load an extended cylinder and its rod can carry before the rod buckles; it falls as stroke and extended length increase and rises with rod diameter. Push force is working pressure multiplied by the piston (bore) area.
extraFacts.source: Standard mechanics (Euler column buckling; force = pressure x area), as applied in maker hydraulic cylinder catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Pin-to-pin (retracted) length is the distance between the two mounting pin centres with the cylinder fully retracted; extended length is the retracted length plus the stroke.
extraFacts.source: Maker cylinder catalogues; Indus guide to hydraulic cylinder mounting styles

extraFacts.fact: SAE ORB (O-ring boss) ports use a straight thread sealed by an O-ring; NPT ports are tapered pipe threads that seal on the thread.
HS 8412.21 covers hydraulic power engines and motors, linear acting (hydraulic cylinders).

NFPA tie-rod hydraulic cylinders follow the NFPA T3.6.7 mounting-dimension standard, so cylinders of the same bore, rod and mounting style are dimensionally interchangeable between makers that build to it.
extraFacts.source: NFPA T3.6.7 (hydraulic fluid power cylinders, mounting dimensions)

extraFacts.fact: Tie-rod cylinders clamp the end caps onto a barrel tube with external tie rods and can be dismantled for seal replacement; welded-body cylinders have the end caps welded to the tube and are compact and sealed against dismantling.
extraFacts.source: Indus guide: welded vs tie-rod hydraulic cylinders; maker cylinder catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Telescopic cylinders extend in nested stages; each added stage lengthens the stroke for a given retracted length, and a single-acting telescopic cylinder retracts under load or gravity rather than by oil pressure.
extraFacts.source: Indus guide: telescopic hydraulic cylinders; Enerpac telescopic cylinder catalogue
